To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ultra-high-energy cosmic rays, accelerated in the jets or active galactic nuclei (AGN) and accumulating in the magnetic fields of the surrounding galaxies, can initiate gamma-ray halos in AGN.

(i) the γ-ray halo of Cygnus A can be detected with the Fermi LAT and possibly ground-based γ-ray instruments if UHECRs originate in radio galaxies and (ii) the detection of the γ-ray halo will provide information about the UHECR spectrum and composition in the vicinity of Cygnus  A. The

the gamma rays from ultra-high-energy cosmic rays in Cygnus-A should be detectable by Fermi and possibly by ground-based gamma-ray telescopes if active galactic nuclei are the sources of ultra-high-energy cosmic-rays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the physics and astrophysics of cosmic rays.
the production of high-energy gamma rays from ultra-high-energy cosmic rays in the vicinity of powerful radio galaxies.
the study of the origin of cosmic rays and their interaction with the interstellar medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed gamma rays from Cygnus A are consistent with a model of ultra high energy cosmic rays from this source.
there is no compelling evidence for the existence of a γ-ray halo in Cygnus A.
The Fermi-LAT data do not support the hypothesis that Cygnus A is a UHECR accelerator, but they are not inconsistent with it either.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the detection of a halo of γ-ray emission around Cyg A would provide evidence for a new mechanism for the acceleration of UHECR to the highest energies and for a new source of high-energy γ-ray emission.
the detection of the γ-ray synchronron halo would provide evidence for the origin of UHECR in active galactic nuclei.
we are able to show the existence of a gamma-ray halo around Cygnus A, which can be used to constrain the UHECR source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
UHECRs can produce detectable γ-ray halos around radio galaxies and, thus, the γ-ray halos may be used to probe the sources of UHCRs.
γ-ray telescopes can be used to test the hypothesis that powerful radio galaxies are the source of UHECR acceleration.
the detection of γ-ray halos around powerful radio galaxies could serve as a signature for the acceleration of UHECR in their jets.
